d: Complete binary tree providing O(1) access to min/max element and O(log n) insertions.

p: A Heap is a complete binary tree implemented as an array. A Min-Heap guarantees the root is the smallest element. Python's `heapq` provides Min-Heap functions.
Push: Add to end of array, bubble up. O(log N)
Pop: Swap root with last element, pop array, bubble down root. O(log N)
Heapify: Turns an array into a heap in O(N) time.

import heapq

arr = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
heapq.heapify(arr) # O(N)

heapq.heappush(arr, 2) # O(log N)
smallest = heapq.heappop(arr) # O(log N) -> Returns 1
Time: O(N) heapify, O(log N) push/pop. Space: O(1) if heapifying in-place.

Min-Heap (Root is smallest):
        [ 1 ]
       /     \
    [ 3 ]   [ 6 ]
   /    \
[ 5 ]  [ 9 ]
